newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up on Monday on short-covering but trade was dull with trading suspended in the world market for Easter, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 23,960 yuan ($2,888) per tonne, up 20 yuan. It opened at 23,950 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 23,930 and a high of 23,980 yuan per tonne.
April rose 50 to 23,510, May was unchanged at 23,600, June 20 to 23,800, August 20 to 23,950, September 100 to 23,900 and the first listed October contract ended at 23,800 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 10,670 tonnes from 22,750 tonnes.
Copper opened little changed and moved in a narrow range for most of the session.
Traders said most investos stayed on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news whilethe day's trading was dominated by the presence of speculators.
"Many investors are waiting for a hint of what direction the market will take once trading on the London Metal Exchange resumes," a trader said.
The London Metal Exchange is closed for Easter until Tuesday.
Traders expected copper trading to be dull on Tuesday, too.
Aluminium ended unchanged from last Friday's close. April closed unchanged at 16,150 yuan ($1,946) per tonne, May 16,450 and June 16,700.
Combined volume rose to 1,480 tonnes from 460 tonnes.
